functions.name: highwayhash::HighwayHashT
functions.signature: template <class State, typename Result> void highwayhash::HighwayHashT(State* state, const char* bytes, size_t size, Result* hash)
functions.description: Computes a HighwayHash of the given byte range using the provided hashing state. Callers supply a state initialized with a key, the data pointer and length, and a result buffer (64-, 128-, or 256-bit) to receive the final hash. Intended for single-shot hashing of a contiguous buffer; for incremental hashing of multiple ranges, either replicate this logic using State::Update/Finalize or use HighwayHashCatT.
requirements: state must be a valid pointer to a State (typically HHStateT<...>) that has been initialized with an HHKey.
bytes must point to at least size readable bytes; the pointer may be unaligned.
size specifies exactly how many bytes are hashed; the function does not read beyond bytes + size.
hash must point to writable storage for a Result compatible with State::Finalize (commonly HHResult64/128/256).
Must be compiled with flags appropriate for the chosen implementation/State (as required by the target-specific HighwayHash implementation).

functions.name: highwayhash::HighwayHashCatT::Append
functions.signature: template <TargetBits Target> void highwayhash::HighwayHashCatT<Target>::Append(const char* bytes, size_t num_bytes)
functions.description: Appends a byte range to the incremental hash. Internally buffers partial packets and updates the state for full packets. Can be called repeatedly before Finalize. There are no alignment requirements. Note: hashing sequences like {"A", ""} and {"", "A"} produce the same result unless you include a disambiguator (e.g., lengths).
requirements: If num_bytes == 0 the call has no effect.
When num_bytes > 0, bytes must point to at least num_bytes readable bytes within [bytes, bytes + num_bytes).
bytes may be unaligned; alignment is not required.
May be called multiple times before Finalize; order of calls affects the hash only through the concatenation of contents (empty ranges do not affect the result).

functions.name: highwayhash::InstructionSets::Run
functions.signature:
template <template <TargetBits> class Func, typename... Args>
static HH_INLINE TargetBits Run(Args&&... args);
functions.description: Detects the best supported target for the current CPU and invokes Func<Target>::operator()(args...) for that target, returning the chosen HH_TARGET_* bit. Dispatch overhead is low (~4 cycles) and should typically be hoisted out of hot loops. On unsupported architectures or when no accelerated targets are available, it invokes the portable specialization.
requirements: Func must be a template taking a single non-type template parameter of type TargetBits (e.g., template <TargetBits T> struct MyFunc { void operator()(...) const; }).

For the target actually selected at runtime (e.g., HH_TARGET_AVX2, HH_TARGET_SSE41, HH_TARGET_VSX, HH_TARGET_NEON, or HH_TARGET_Portable), a definition of Func<that_target>::operator()(Args...) must be available at link time.
The provided arguments must be valid for and acceptable to the selected Func<Target>::operator()(Args...), including const/volatile and value category (perfect-forwarded).
If multiple targets may be selected at runtime on a given build, all corresponding Func<target> specializations intended to be callable in that build must be defined to avoid link or ODR issues.
Caller should not assume Run will call more than one specialization; exactly one Func<Target> is invoked per call.
The return value is the HH_TARGET_* bit of the invoked specialization and should be checked if the caller needs to know which specialization ran.

functions.name: highwayhash::InstructionSets::RunAll
functions.signature:
template <template <TargetBits> class Func, typename... Args>
static HH_INLINE TargetBits RunAll(Args&&... args);
functions.description: Invokes Func<Target>::operator()(args...) for each supported target on the current CPU, including HH_TARGET_Portable, and returns the union bitmask of the HH_TARGET_* values that were run. Useful for initializing or validating all available implementations.
requirements: Func must be a template taking a single non-type template parameter of type TargetBits and provide operator()(Args...) for every target that may be run on the current CPU, including HH_TARGET_Portable.
All invoked Func<Target> specializations must be defined and linkable; otherwise linkage errors will occur.
Arguments must be valid for every Func<Target>::operator()(Args...) that will be called in this process (they are perfect-forwarded).
Caller should expect Func<Target> to be invoked zero or more times for accelerated targets depending on Supported(), and always at least once for HH_TARGET_Portable.
The returned TargetBits value is the same as Supported() for the current build/CPU and represents all targets that were invoked.

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator targets arbitrary binary data consumed by the fuzz stubs.
# The fuzzers use FUZZ_PARAM_STR and various integers to select sizes/offsets.
# Our strategy: produce a binary blob that contains multiple interesting regions
# and lengths so that when the fuzzer slices into it (choose size, offsets,
# or pad to 8-byte boundaries), it will still be valid and exercise different
# internal paths: sizes 0..7 (SipHash padding tails), exact 8/16 boundaries,
# large blocks, unaligned prefixes, and mixed byte patterns.
# The result is a self-contained bytes object <= 4096 bytes.

_GOLDEN_RATIO_64 = 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15


def _p64(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<Q', x & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)


def _pattern_block(tag: int, size: int, seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed ^ (tag * 0x5851F42D4C957F2D))
    # Mix of runs, incrementing bytes, and random noise
    out = bytearray()
    modes = ["zeros", "ff", "inc", "dec", "rand", "alt", "wordrep"]
    i = 0
    while i < size:
        mode = rnd.choice(modes)
        run = 1 + rnd.randrange(min(64, max(1, size - i)))
        if mode == "zeros":
            out.extend(b"\x00" * run)
        elif mode == "ff":
            out.extend(b"\xFF" * run)
        elif mode == "inc":
            start = rnd.randrange(256)
            for k in range(run):
                out.append((start + k) & 0xFF)
        elif mode == "dec":
            start = rnd.randrange(256)
            for k in range(run):
                out.append((start - k) & 0xFF)
        elif mode == "rand":
            out.extend(bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(run)))
        elif mode == "alt":
            b0 = rnd.randrange(256)
            b1 = b0 ^ 0xFF
            for k in range(run):
                out.append(b0 if (k & 1) == 0 else b1)
        elif mode == "wordrep":
            # repeat a 64-bit word with interesting bits
            w = (_GOLDEN_RATIO_64 * (1 + rnd.randrange(17))) ^ (seed << (rnd.randrange(8)))
            chunk = _p64(w)
            reps = (run + 7) // 8
            out.extend(chunk * reps)
        i += run
    return bytes(out[:size])


def _make_header(sections: List[Tuple[int, int]]) -> bytes:
    # Simple header to give structure for potential consumers:
    # magic(4) version(2) count(2) then entries of: tag(4) offset(4) size(4)
    header = bytearray()
    header.extend(b"HWHH")
    header.extend(struct.pack('<H', 1))
    header.extend(struct.pack('<H', len(sections)))
    # placeholder for entries filled by caller with proper offsets
    return bytes(header)


def _align(b: bytearray, align: int) -> None:
    pad = (-len(b)) & (align - 1)
    if pad:
        b.extend(b"\x00" * pad)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide total size budget <= 4096
    budget = rnd.randrange(512, 4096 + 1)

    # Plan sections with sizes chosen to exercise 0..7 tails and multiples of 8
    small_tails = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
    exact_blocks = [8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64]
    var_large = [rnd.randrange(65, 512), rnd.randrange(256, 1024)]

    sizes = []
    # ensure coverage of tails by creating base sizes then plus tail
    base = rnd.randrange(0, 256) & ~7  # multiple of 8
    for t in small_tails:
        sizes.append(base + t)
    sizes.extend(exact_blocks)
    sizes.extend(var_large)

    # Trim based on budget per-section assembly
    sections: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []  # (tag, size)
    total_planned = 0
    for idx, s in enumerate(sizes):
        if total_planned + s > budget:
            break
        sections.append((0x100 + idx, s))
        total_planned += s

    # Always include a zero-length and a moderate section if room
    if total_planned + 0 <= budget:
        sections.insert(0, (0x001, 0))
    if total_planned + 128 <= budget:
        sections.append((0x2FF, 128))

    # Build buffer: header + directory + payloads
    # We’ll write a simple directory after header for discoverability by fuzzer slices
    header = _make_header(sections)
    directory_entry_size = 12  # tag, offset, size

    buf = bytearray()
    buf.extend(header)
    # Reserve space for directory entries
    dir_start = len(buf)
    buf.extend(b"\x00" * (len(sections) * directory_entry_size))

    payload_offsets: List[int] = []

    # Add some unaligned padding before first payload to encourage unaligned starts
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        buf.extend(b"PAD!")
        if rnd.random() < 0.5:
            buf.extend(b"\xAA\x55\xAA")

    # Payloads
    for i, (tag, size) in enumerate(sections):
        # Mix alignment: sometimes align to 8, sometimes not
        if rnd.random() < 0.5:
            _align(buf, 8)
        else:
            # add 0..7 bytes to ensure unaligned packet boundaries
            buf.extend(b"U" * rnd.randrange(0, 8))
        payload_offsets.append(len(buf))
        block = _pattern_block(tag, size, seed ^ (i * 0xA5A5A5A5)) if size > 0 else b""
        buf.extend(block)
        # Add sentinel between sections to allow larger reads safely up to next 8 boundary
        _align(buf, 8)

    # Fill directory
    dir_bytes = bytearray()
    for (tag, size), off in zip(sections, payload_offsets):
        dir_bytes.extend(struct.pack('<III', tag & 0xFFFFFFFF, off & 0xFFFFFFFF, size & 0xFFFFFFFF))
    buf[dir_start:dir_start + len(dir_bytes)] = dir_bytes

    # Footer with some repeated hashes/keys seeds for the stubs creating keys from integers
    # Provide multiple 64-bit words that FUZZ_PARAM(uint64_t) may pick from when slicing
    _align(buf, 8)
    key_seed_base = rnd.getrandbits(64)
    footer = bytearray()
    for k in range(16):
        footer.extend(_p64(key_seed_base + k * _GOLDEN_RATIO_64))
    buf.extend(footer)

    # Ensure final size cap
    return bytes(buf[:4096])
